title: Diwali Bonus Tax: The ₹15,000 Gift Limit and When Cash Is Fully Taxed
excerpt: Employer gifts in kind are tax-free only below ₹15,000 a year under the new Income-tax Rules, 2026 — cross it and the whole amount is a perquisite. Cash bonuses get no exemption at all.
body:
• Employer gifts, vouchers and tokens in kind are tax-free only while their combined value stays below ₹15,000 in a tax year — at or above that, the entire amount becomes a taxable perquisite, not just the excess.
  • The ₹15,000 limit is new: the Income-tax Rules, 2026 raised it from ₹5,000, effective for tax year 2026-27 (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027).
  • A cash Diwali bonus never qualifies for the exemption. It is salary, taxed at your slab rate with TDS, in whichever regime you choose.
  • Check your payslip: the bonus should appear in salary, any gift above the threshold should appear as a perquisite, and both should flow into your salary TDS certificate — Form 130, which replaces Form 16 from tax year 2026-27.

Diwali is over, and the festive money has landed — a bonus in the bank, a hamper, maybe a shopping voucher. The tax treatment of each is different, and this year one number changed. The rules sit in the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026, which came into effect on April 1, 2026, Mint reported.

The ₹15,000 rule, precisely

For gifts in kind from an employer — hampers, vouchers, tokens, including gifts received by members of an employee's household, on ceremonial occasions or otherwise — the taxable value is nil if the combined value during the tax year is below ₹15,000, according to TaxGuru's summary of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. The limit was raised from ₹5,000 under the previous rules. Two mechanics catch people out. First, the limit is annual, not per festival: a ₹9,000 festive voucher and a ₹5,000 shopping voucher in the same year total ₹14,000 and qualify; anything that takes the year's total to ₹15,000 or beyond ends the exemption. Second, when it ends, it ends completely — the entire amount is treated as a taxable perquisite added to salary, Mint reported, not merely the amount above the threshold.

Cash is always salary

A cash bonus does not qualify for the ₹15,000 exemption at all. It is treated as salary income and taxed at the applicable slab rate, with the employer deducting TDS through payroll. The same applies to anything convertible into money, such as gift cheques. A bonus can also interact with the new regime's rebate: salaried employees get a standard deduction of ₹75,000, so salary income of up to ₹12.75 lakh may result in zero tax where the rebate conditions are met and there is no other taxable income. Mint's example: an employee earning ₹12 lakh who receives a ₹50,000 Diwali bonus has taxable income of ₹11.75 lakh after the standard deduction and remains eligible for the full rebate; if the bonus pushes gross salary beyond ₹12.75 lakh, taxable income exceeds ₹12 lakh and tax may be triggered, with marginal relief potentially limiting the additional amount.

Gifts from everyone else

Outside the employer relationship, a different provision applies — Section 92(2)(m) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, corresponding to Section 56(2)(x) of the 1961 Act. Monetary gifts and specified movable property from non-relatives are tax-free only up to ₹50,000 in aggregate per year; above that, the entire amount is taxable as income from other sources. Gifts from specified relatives — spouse, siblings, parents, lineal ascendants and descendants, and their spouses — are exempt without limit, as are gifts received on your own marriage or under a will.

What to check before you file

Employers account for taxable amounts through payroll, and they should appear in your salary TDS certificate — Form 130, which replaces Form 16 for salary TDS certificates from tax year 2026-27, Mint reported. Verify that a cash bonus is included in salary, that any gift at or above the threshold is recorded as a perquisite, and that the TDS figures match your payslips before filing in July 2027. Final liability depends on total income, the regime chosen, and eligible deductions — Mint's explainer, at LiveMint, is informational, and a qualified tax adviser remains the right check for individual cases.
